# Niklas Weber — Systems Developer

Niklas Weber is a systems programmer at 42 Heilbronn specializing in C, Go, and low-level optimization.

## Projects

### Transcendence Casino
Real-time multiplayer online casino — Blackjack, Texas Hold'em Poker, and a slot machine. Live at https://transcendence.nweber.me.
Three-tier architecture: Go + Gin backend, standalone C++ game engine over gRPC, React/TypeScript frontend. Hand-rolled WebSocket hub (topic fan-out, multi-tab presence). Exact decimal money math with row-locked transactions and an immutable audit ledger. Prometheus + Grafana monitoring with six dashboards and Discord alerting.
Source: https://github.com/nweber23/transcendence

### 42 ELO Leaderboard
Go + PostgreSQL ranking system for 42 school. Live at https://eloleaderboard.de.
Key achievement: 30ms average response time, 99.9% uptime. Composite indexes, Redis caching, Go goroutines for concurrent match processing.
Source: https://github.com/nweber23/42_ELO_Leaderboard

### miniRT
High-performance raytracer in C. SIMD vectorization (SSE/AVX), cache-efficient structure-of-arrays layout, tile-based multi-threaded rendering.
Key achievement: 120+ FPS, an 80x improvement over baseline (1920x1080, complex scene).
Source: https://github.com/nweber23/miniRT

### minishell
POSIX-compliant shell in C implementing fork/exec, pipe chaining, redirections, signals (SIGCHLD with sigaction), and a recursive-descent parser.
Source: https://github.com/nweber23/minishell

## Writing

### Why I keep building from scratch: process handling, WebSocket hubs, and .obj parsers
A case for hand-rolling the parts of a system that matter — minishell's process handling, a WebSocket hub, an .obj parser — and reaching for a library everywhere else.
https://nweber.me/writing/build-from-scratch.html

### Getting Elo leaderboard queries under 100ms: indexes, caching, and profiling instead of guessing
How the 42 Elo Leaderboard hit 30ms average response times — composite indexes matched to actual query shapes, Redis for derived stats that don't need recomputing on every read, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE over intuition.
https://nweber.me/writing/elo-query-performance.html

### gRPC versus REST: picking protocols at the Transcendence service boundary
Why Transcendence uses REST/WebSocket at the browser-facing edge but gRPC/protobuf between the Go backend and the C++ game engine, and what that split actually buys.
https://nweber.me/writing/grpc-vs-rest.html

### Triangulating arbitrary polygons with ear clipping over a Newell-normal plane
How the 3D Go Renderer triangulates arbitrary .obj faces — including concave, non-planar, and degenerate polygons — using ear clipping projected onto each face's Newell normal.
https://nweber.me/writing/ear-clipping.html
